submission.justification: No project document or tool output gives the FPGA latency of any candidate, so the 4.0 us hard limit cannot be verified for any of them. Algorithm-L2 (fixed-window sum) is the only candidate with no iterative clustering or learned calibration stage, so it is the most likely to fit the latency budget, and I recommend it on that basis. Its emulated signal efficiency at the 8 kHz allocation is 74.6% at 35 GeV (74.4% at 30 GeV). Algorithm-L1 gives higher efficiency (92.9% at 35 GeV) but its iterative topological clustering is the most likely to exceed 4.0 us, and I could not confirm otherwise, so I did not recommend it. Algorithm-L3 (83.2% at 35 GeV, 85.9% at 30 GeV) uses sliding-window clustering with learned calibration; its latency is also unverified. Before adoption, the FPGA latency of L2 must be measured and confirmed under 4.0 us. If L1 or L3 can be shown to fit the budget, either would give substantially higher efficiency at the same rate.
